title: Merged-worktree sweep refuses forever when git-lfs is configured globally
description:
## Symptom

Merged branches never leave the sidebar. `thegn merge sweep` reports every candidate as kept and ends with `Swept 0 merged worktree(s).`:

```
- kept fix/push-ci-20260916 - /tmp/thegn-push-ci-20260916: configured Git clean/process filters require explicit cleanup
- kept tg/review-audit-host-notice - ...: configured Git clean/process filters require explicit cleanup
```

`--force` does not help: this refusal is independent of the grace period, so there is **no** way to clear the worktrees through thegn. Observed on this machine with 35 merged-but-present worktrees, the oldest 9 days past their `merged_ttl_secs`.

## Cause

`crates/thegn-host/src/merge_cleanup.rs:276-284` refuses cleanup when any `filter.*.clean` / `filter.*.process` key exists:

```rust
let config = git(path, &["config", "--null", "--includes", "--list"])?;
if config.split(..).any(|entry| key.starts_with("filter.")
    && (key.ends_with(".clean") || key.ends_with(".process"))) {
    return Err(unsafe_reason(
        "configured Git clean/process filters require explicit cleanup"));
}
```

`git config --list` includes **global and system** config. Installing git-lfs anywhere on the machine (here: home-manager, so it is in `~/.gitconfig`) sets `filter.lfs.clean` and `filter.lfs.process` globally and permanently disables merged-worktree cleanup for **every** repository - including repositories that contain no LFS files at all.

On this repository:

* `git ls-files -z ':(attr:filter)'` returns **0 files**.
* There is no `.gitattributes` anywhere in the tree.

So no path here is routed through any filter, yet cleanup is refused.

## Why the check exists (keep the intent)

The comment is correct about the risk: `git status` can run clean/process drivers while refreshing index content, and a filter may be slow, hang, or have side effects. The refusal should stay - it is the *predicate* that is wrong.

## Suggested fix

Refuse only when a tracked path in **this** worktree actually has a `filter` attribute, rather than when a filter driver is merely configured somewhere. Git answers this directly with pathspec magic:

```
git ls-files -z ':(attr:filter)'
```

Non-empty => refuse exactly as today. Empty => no path can invoke a driver, so `status` is safe and cleanup may proceed.

Keep the existing data-only handling (config values are never logged) and keep every other refusal (`skip-worktree`/`assume-unchanged`, submodules, etc.) unchanged.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] A repository with a globally configured but locally unused filter driver sweeps normally.
- [ ] A repository with at least one tracked path carrying a `filter` attribute still refuses, with the same message.
- [ ] The probe cannot itself invoke a filter driver.
- [ ] Tests cover: global-only filter config + no attributes; a `.gitattributes` assigning `filter=lfs` to a tracked path; and an empty/attribute-free repo.
- [ ] The refusal message names what was found, so the operator can tell "this repo uses filters" from "some filter exists on this machine".

## Separately observed

Four worktrees are kept for a different reason - `landed commit identity is missing` (`tg/spark-radar`, `tg/bold-petal`, `tg/keen-marble`, `tg/bold-mango`). That is a distinct cause and is not covered by this issue.
